title: Experimental and theoretical investigations on the phase stability and mechanical properties of Cr7Mn25Co9Ni23Cu36 high-entropy alloy
notes: No introduction, methods or results text in the packet (captions_plus_linked_text), so HYP, DES and PRC are 'text' with requires_unseen. Two spine branches leave the anneal: the phase-evolution branch (two FCC up to 600 C -> kinetic MEC -> sigma at 800 C) and the nanoprecipitate branch; the 1000 C arm (n10, n17, n20) is kept off-spine as a side branch and rejoins at n18. Packet/paper defects found by opening the images: (1) the F1a and F1e crops each carry two whole panels (a+b and e+f), and the F5a crop carries a+b, so three of the offered panel ids are two-panel crops; (2) F1d labels one region 'FCC 1 Cu-rich region' while the same panel calls FCC_1 'Co and Cr-rich' - F4 and the text make FCC_1 Cu-poor, so one arrow is mislabelled (a1); (3) the F5a and F5b insets carry 50 um scale bars although they are zoom-ins of panels with 30 and 40 um bars; (4) F5 shows six panels for the five times given in the caption (c and d are both 8 h, at 30 and 10 um); sigma is only visible in the 10 um-bar panels, so the 8 h onset is a detection threshold (a2); (5) F1c carries a stray '(a)' panel letter as well as '(c)'; (6) the packet lists no OCR at all for the whole-figure crops F3, F4 and F6, although F4 carries a printed composition table; (7) F3 reads a sigma solvus of ~870 C against the text's 'approximately 850 C'; (8) the text's 401 and 700 MPa are the as-cast points, not the 200 C points as the sentence implies; (9) the text says only that strengths 'decreased' at 1000 C, whereas F7a/F7b show near-elastic fracture at ~110 MPa with 0 % elongation; (10) F8 cannot resolve the claimed 4.5 -> 3.5 nm refinement (a3), and the Co map F2d shows no enrichment at the sigma particles although the text gives sigma ~27 at.% Co.

nodes.label: Phase stability of the Cu-rich non-equiatomic Cr7Mn25Co9Ni23Cu36 HEA on annealing, and its effect on tensile properties, is unestablished

requires_unseen: introduction and abstract are not in the packet; the gap is read from the title and the F3/F5 linked text

nodes.label: Annealing temperature and holding time should change which phases the alloy contains and therefore its tensile behaviour
Cr7Mn25Co9Ni23Cu36 HEA, a non-equiatomic Cu-rich composition that solidifies with two FCC solid solutions

requires_unseen: the nominal composition Cr7Mn25Co9Ni23Cu36 is given only in the captions and linked text

nodes.label: Sweep heat-treatment temperature over 200, 400, 600, 800 and 1000 C for 2 h, and holding time over 4-12 h at 600 C
Combine CALPHAD equilibrium calculation (Thermo-Calc, TCHEA) and DFT total-energy calculation with SEM/TEM/EDS and tensile testing

requires_unseen: Thermo-Calc, the TCHEA database and the DFT set-up are named only in the F3 and F6 linked text

nodes.label: Cast the alloy on a water-cooled copper hearth; solidification and cooling to room temperature take only a few minutes

requires_unseen: the casting route and the few-minute cooling are stated only in the F5 linked text

nodes.label: Anneal cast samples for 2 h at 200, 400, 600, 800 and 1000 C, and for 4, 6, 8, 10 and 12 h at 600 C
As-cast and after 2 h at 200-600 C the alloy holds only two FCC solid solutions, FCC_1 (Co,Cr-rich) and FCC_2 (Cu-rich), with no intermetallic

attrs.image_note: SEM shows a dendritic two-contrast structure in all four states and no bright second-phase particles; that the two regions are FCC comes from the text and ref [31], not from the SEM contrast
requires_unseen: FCC crystal structure of the two regions and the FCC_1 / FCC_2 naming come from the linked text and ref [31]

nodes.label: In the as-cast state FCC_1 is Cu-poor and rich in Co and Cr (Cu 9.5 at.%); FCC_2 is Cu-rich (Cu 44.5 at.%)
Sigma sits as chains of discrete particles on the interdendritic boundaries, absent from the dendrite interiors, ranging from ~0.2 to ~1 um

attrs.image_note: F1e inset (2 um bar) shows a bead-like chain; F2a shows two lenticular laths ~0.5-1 um long in one grain boundary region

nodes.label: At 600 C sigma is first detected after 8 h and its area fraction keeps growing to 12 h

attrs.image_note: 8 h shows one small cluster, 12 h shows particles over most of the field at the same 10 um bar

nodes.label: Calculated equilibrium: FCC_2 is primary and near-constant, FCC_1 exists only above ~690 C, sigma is stable below ~870 C

attrs.image_note: so at 600 C equilibrium is FCC_2 + ~10% sigma with no FCC_1, the opposite of the 2 h experiment

nodes.label: DFT gives ferrimagnetic FCC the lowest total energy, below paramagnetic FCC and every HCP and BCC state

attrs.image_note: energies referenced to FCC-FM; minima at Wigner-Seitz radius ~2.67-2.70 Bohr

nodes.label: Sigma precipitation is set jointly by the thermodynamic driving force and sluggish solid-state diffusion, so 2 h below 800 C is too short to nucleate it

requires_unseen: the sluggish-kinetics argument is stated in the F5 linked text

nodes.label: Finer, denser nanoprecipitates raise the obstacle density against dislocation glide, so strength rises while ductility falls
Coarse, inhomogeneously distributed sigma particles concentrate stress and nucleate cracks, cutting strength and ductility together

requires_unseen: the paper attributes the drop to sigma being inhomogeneously distributed and varying in size up to several hundred nm (F7/F8 linked text)

nodes.label: Cu segregation zones formed at 1000 C act as soft, weakly bonded regions that trigger premature fracture

requires_unseen: the attribution to Cu segregation zones is stated in the F7 linked text; no evidence links a fracture site to such a zone

nodes.label: Yield and ultimate tensile strength rise to a maximum at 600 C (~580 and ~825 MPa) while elongation falls from ~35 to ~22 %

attrs.image_note: text quotes 401 -> 581 MPa and 700 -> 829 MPa; the 401 and 700 MPa values are the as-cast points, not the 200 C points, which read ~440 and ~700 MPa on F7b

nodes.label: Annealing at 800 C drops the alloy to ~530 MPa UTS, ~305 MPa yield and ~15 % elongation
After 1000 C the alloy is essentially brittle: it fractures near ~110 MPa below 0.5 % strain, with elongation plotted at 0 %

attrs.image_note: the text says only that both strengths 'decreased'; F7a and F7b show a near-elastic fracture, a far stronger statement

nodes.label: The alloy keeps a usable strength-ductility balance only for anneals up to 600 C; anneals at 800 and 1000 C disqualify it

attrs.condition: room-temperature tension after a 2 h anneal

nodes.label: Sigma formation is deleterious to the tensile properties of this HEA
The CALPHAD phase compositions (FCC_1 Cu-poor and Co,Cr-rich; FCC_2 Cu-rich) agree with the as-cast EDS measurements

pairs.cause: Heat treatment at 800 C for 2 h
pairs.effect: Formation of Cr- and Co-rich sigma phase with tetragonal structure
pairs.note: n7 produces the 800 C state and n9 is the Cr-rich tetragonal sigma claim, evidenced by o3 (labelled chains), o4 (indexed tetragonal SAED) and o6 (Cr map). The graph does not support the 'Co-rich' half: o6's image_note records that the Co, Mn and Ni maps show no visible enrichment at the particles, even though the text gives sigma ~27 at.% Co

pairs.effect: Decrease in yield strength, ultimate tensile strength and elongation to fracture
pairs.note: n9 -> n14 causes, with n16 (coarse, inhomogeneous sigma concentrates stress) explaining it and k4 as the premise; n19 is the same conclusion. The graph's numbers are read from F7 (~530 MPa UTS, ~305 MPa yield, ~15 %) and match MatMech's 530/303/15

pairs.cause: Heat treatment at 600 C for extended durations (>8 h)
pairs.effect: Delayed formation of sigma phase due to sluggish solid-state diffusion kinetics
pairs.note: s3 (first detected at 8 h, growing to 12 h) supports n12, the joint thermodynamics-plus-sluggish-diffusion pathway, with s4 (CALPHAD: sigma stable below ~870 C) and k5 as the other inputs. The graph adds an audit MatMech does not have: a2 records that sigma is visible only in the two 10 um-bar panels, so '8 h' is a detection threshold at the magnification shown, not a measured incubation time
